History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
29-year-old woman with one-week history of intermittent fever, sweats, myalgia, nausea, and fatigue after recent travel to rural Vietnam; requires urgent in-person assessment and malaria screen.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Fever for 7 days with alternating hot and cold episodes, profuse sweating (including night sweats), generalized muscle aches, nausea with reduced appetite, and marked fatigue.  
• Onset/progression: Began ~1 week ago; persistent despite regular paracetamol/ibuprofen (partial, temporary relief). No clear pattern to temperature fluctuations.  
• Associated symptoms: Myalgia, nausea, night sweats. No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, rash, joint swelling (except chronic back pain), dysuria, urinary frequency, or increased headaches beyond baseline.  
• Review of systems:  
  – HEENT: Chronic centralized tension-type headaches related to screen use; no new headache features. No ear pain, sore throat, or visual complaints noted.  
  – Respiratory: Denies cough or shortness of breath.  
  – Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations reported.  
  – GI: No diarrhea. Nausea present; poor oral intake.  
  – GU: No urinary symptoms.  
  – Skin: No rash.  
  – Neuro: No neck stiffness; no focal deficits reported.  
• Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; daily malaria prophylaxis taken (specific drug/dose not recalled) plus an additional unspecified tablet. Activities included trekking, cycling, river and farmland exposure in rural regions.  
• Exposures: Works as a nurse; up-to-date occupational vaccines (incl. Hep B).

Past Medical History:
• Chronic mechanical back pain related to prolonged sitting/poor posture; under physiotherapy.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Seroxat (paroxetine) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Ibuprofen – OTC, recommended dose; exact schedule not documented.  
• Paracetamol – OTC, recommended dose; exact schedule not documented.  
• Malaria prophylaxis during travel – specific agent/dose not recalled (completed daily regimen).  

Allergies:
• Pollen (hay fever).  
• No medication allergies reported.

Social History:
• Occupation: Nurse; currently struggling at work due to fatigue.  
• Smoking: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: Moderate intake (details not provided).  
• Exercise: Moderate activity a few times per week.  
• Vaccinations: Up to date, including Hepatitis B.

Family History:
• Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.  
• No other familial illnesses noted.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed during teleconsult; to be completed in clinic.)

Investigations:
• Planned:  
  – Thick and thin blood films for malaria.  
  – Full blood count, inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP/ESR), and other relevant labs per examining clinician.  
• No results available yet.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Pyrexia of unknown origin post-travel; rule out malaria and other tropical infections.  
  • Arrange same-day in-person assessment at central London clinic (or local ED if more convenient).  
  • Perform full physical examination and vitals.  
  • Order thick & thin malaria films, FBC, inflammatory markers, and additional blood tests as indicated.  
  • Consider further infectious work-up based on examination (e.g., blood cultures, liver/renal panels).  

Issue 2: Work fitness.  
  • Advise patient not to return to work until evaluation complete and cause identified/treated.  

Issue 3: Symptomatic relief.  
  • Continue paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed (within recommended limits).  
  • Encourage adequate hydration despite reduced appetite.  

General Plan items:  
• Administrative: Doctor to document consultation findings and requested investigations; admin team to schedule urgent clinic appointment and provide contact details.  
• Follow-up: Results review and further management to follow once investigations complete.

Quality checks:

Missing expected elements:
• Vitals, physical examination findings, and laboratory values not available.  
• Detailed medication list (dose, route, frequency) incomplete.  
• No documentation of contraception, menstrual history, or mood despite paroxetine use.

Internal conflicts:
• None noted.

Transcript quality:
• Clear; minor overlaps but clinically relevant information captured.
